def-yangian-gl-n-rtt-presentation:
## Definition

Fix an integer $N\ge2$, the field $\mathbb C$, and the ordered vector-space basis $e_1,\ldots,e_N$ of $V_N=\mathbb C^N$. The matrix units $E_{ij}$ have the convention of [[def-matrix-units]], and $\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ means $M_N(\mathbb C)$ with the commutator bracket. Tensor products are over $\mathbb C$ and use the fixed finite tensor convention of [[def-hh-rational-spectral-r-matrix]]; the elementary tensors form the basis supplied by [[thm-tensor-product-basis-from-bases]].

Define the flip $P_N\in\operatorname{End}(V_N\otimes V_N)$ by $P_N(e_a\otimes e_b)=e_b\otimes e_a$, and set $R_N(x)=xI+iP_N$, where $i^2=-1$. For $V_N^{\otimes3}$, $P_{12},P_{13},P_{23}$ swap the indicated positions and $R_{ab}(x)=xI+iP_{ab}$. Products mean composition, with the rightmost factor applied first.

Let $t_{ij}^{(r)}$ for $1\le i,j\le N$ and $r\ge1$ be generators, and put $t_{ij}(u)=\delta_{ij}+\sum_{r\ge1}t_{ij}^{(r)}u^{-r}$ and $T_0(u)=\sum_{i,j}E_{ij}^{(0)}\otimes t_{ij}(u)$. On two auxiliary copies of $V_N$, define $T_1(u)=\sum_{i,j}E_{ij}\otimes I\otimes t_{ij}(u)$ and $T_2(v)=\sum_{i,j}I\otimes E_{ij}\otimes t_{ij}(v)$, with the third tensor position the coefficient space. The RTT Yangian $Y_i(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ is the unital associative $\mathbb C$-algebra on these generators modulo the coefficientwise formal-series relation

$$R_{12}(u-v)T_1(u)T_2(v)=T_2(v)T_1(u)R_{12}(u-v).$$

Here the relation means that every coefficient vanishes after expanding each $t_{ij}$ at $u=v=\infty$.

The normalization is rational and difference-form. At $N=2$ its $R$-family is exactly the existing finite supplier [[def-hh-rational-spectral-r-matrix]]; this definition uses that carrier for the rank-two instance and introduces no second $\mathbb C^2$ model.

The proposed coproduct and counit are $\Delta(t_{ij}(u))=\sum_k t_{ik}(u)\otimes t_{kj}(u)$ and $\epsilon(t_{ij}(u))=\delta_{ij}$. The formal antipode is $S(T_0(u))=T_0(u)^{-1}$. Their well-definedness and Hopf identities are proved in [[prop-yangian-gl-n-rtt-hopf-structure]].
lem-yangian-rtt-component-commutator-for:
## Statement

For the presentation in [[def-yangian-gl-n-rtt-presentation]], set $x=u-v$. For every $1\le i,j,k,l\le N$, its matrix RTT relation is equivalent coefficientwise to

$$x[t_{ij}(u),t_{kl}(v)]=i\bigl(t_{kj}(v)t_{il}(u)-t_{kj}(u)t_{il}(v)\bigr).$$
prop-yangian-gl-n-rtt-hopf-structure:
## Statement

For the algebra of [[def-yangian-gl-n-rtt-presentation]], the coefficientwise assignments into the ordinary algebraic tensor product

$$\Delta(t_{ij}(u))=\sum_{k=1}^N t_{ik}(u)\otimes t_{kj}(u),\qquad \epsilon(t_{ij}(u))=\delta_{ij},\qquad S(T_0(u))=T_0(u)^{-1}$$

define a coassociative coproduct, counit, and antipode. Thus they make $Y_i(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ a Hopf algebra. The inverse is the formal matrix inverse at $u=\infty$.
def-yangian-evaluation-module:
## Definition

Let $N\ge2$, let $\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)=M_N(\mathbb C)$ with commutator bracket, and write $E_{ij}$ for its matrix units from [[def-matrix-units]]. For a left $\mathfrak{gl}_N$-module $W$ with action $\rho$ and a parameter $a\in\mathbb C$, define the candidate evaluation module $W(a)$ by the generating-series action

$$t_{ij}(u)\longmapsto \delta_{ij}I_W-\frac{i\rho(E_{ij})}{u-a},$$

where $(u-a)^{-1}=u^{-1}\sum_{r\ge0}(a/u)^r$ is expanded at $u=\infty$. The map defines a Yangian module by [[thm-yangian-evaluation-module-well-defined]]. The rational expression has a pole at $u=a$; the formal series is always defined.

The dual-natural vector space $V_N^\vee$ has basis $f^1,\ldots,f^N$ and the candidate action $\rho^\vee(E_{ij})f^k=-\delta_{ik}f^j$. The following well-definedness theorem verifies that this is a $\mathfrak{gl}_N$-module. On it, the auxiliary matrix of the evaluation series is $I+iP_N/(u-a)$, so the unnormalized Lax matrix $(u-a)T_0(u)$ is $R_N(u-a)=(u-a)I+iP_N$.
thm-yangian-evaluation-module-well-defin:
## Statement

Let $N\ge2$, let $W$ be a left $\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$-module with action $\rho$, and let $a\in\mathbb C$. The assignment in [[def-yangian-evaluation-module]] extends to a representation of $Y_i(\mathfrak{gl}_N)$ on $W(a)$. In particular, the dual-natural action $\rho^\vee(E_{ij})f^k=-\delta_{ik}f^j$ is a $\mathfrak{gl}_N$-representation, and its unnormalized auxiliary Lax matrix equals $R_N(u-a)$.
lem-yangian-rtt-spectral-rescaling:
## Statement

Let $R_i(x)=xI+iP_N$ be the normalization of [[def-yangian-gl-n-rtt-presentation]], and define the standard polynomial Yang matrix $R_0(z)=zI-P_N$. The change of spectral variable $z=iu$, with $\widetilde T(z)=T(-iz)$, converts the RTT relation for $R_i$ to the standard RTT relation for $R_0$. Under this change the evaluation parameter $a$ becomes $ia$.
prop-yangian-rational-r-matrix-yang-baxt:
## Statement

Let $N\ge2$ and let $R_N(x)=xI+iP_N$ be as in [[def-yangian-gl-n-rtt-presentation]]. For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb C$, with $x=a-b$, $y=b-c$, and $z=a-c=x+y$,

$$R_{12}(x)R_{13}(z)R_{23}(y)=R_{23}(y)R_{13}(z)R_{12}(x)$$

on $V_N^{\otimes3}$. Moreover, $R_N(x)^{-1}=(xI-iP_N)/(x^2+1)$ when $x\notin\{i,-i\}$. At $x=i$ the kernel is $\bigwedge^2 V_N$ and the rank is $N(N+1)/2$; at $x=-i$ the kernel is $\operatorname{Sym}^2 V_N$ and the rank is $N(N-1)/2$.
lem-yangian-fundamental-evaluation-inter:
## Statement

Let $N\ge2$, $a,b\in\mathbb C$, and let $W_a=W_b=V_N^\vee$ carry the evaluation actions with parameters $a$ and $b$ from [[def-yangian-evaluation-module]]. On the same ordered space $W_a\otimes W_b$, write $\rho_\Delta$ for the coproduct action and $\rho_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}$ for the action obtained by using $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\sigma\circ\Delta$, where $\sigma(x\otimes y)=y\otimes x$. Their auxiliary generating matrices are respectively $T_{0a}(u)T_{0b}(u)$ and $T_{0b}(u)T_{0a}(u)$. Identify the indexed dual bases with the standard basis when defining $R_{ab}=R_N(a-b)=(a-b)I+iP_N$ on this space. For every generating-series coefficient,

$$\rho_{\Delta}(t_{ij}(u))R_{ab}=R_{ab}\rho_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(t_{ij}(u)).$$

Thus $R_{ab}$ is an intertwining linear map; it is an isomorphism when $a-b\notin\{i,-i\}$. At the two exceptional differences the same intertwining identity holds, but the map is singular as described in [[prop-yangian-rational-r-matrix-yang-baxter-and-invertibility]].
def-yangian-periodic-fundamental-chain:
## Definition

Fix $N\ge2$, a chain length $m\ge1$, and inhomogeneities $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb C$. The quantum space is the finite-dimensional vector space $\mathcal H=(V_N^\vee)^{\otimes m}$, where each factor is the dual-natural evaluation module with its own parameter $a_j$ from [[def-yangian-evaluation-module]]; well-definedness is supplied by [[thm-yangian-evaluation-module-well-defined]]. Let $V_0=V_N$ be an auxiliary copy. Identify the ordered bases $e_i$ and $f^i$ when defining $P_{0j}(e_p\otimes f^q)=e_q\otimes f^p$, with all other quantum factors unchanged, and put

$$L_{0j}(u)= (u-a_j)I+iP_{0j}=R_{0j}(u-a_j),\qquad M_0(u)=L_{01}(u)L_{02}(u)\cdots L_{0m}(u).$$

Products are composition with the rightmost factor applied first. The un-twisted periodic transfer matrix is the polynomial $\tau(u)=\operatorname{tr}_0 M_0(u)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal H)[u]$, where $\operatorname{tr}_0$ is the ordinary matrix trace over the auxiliary basis and does not act on $\mathcal H$. This definition asserts neither Bethe completeness nor Yangian invariance of a periodic Hamiltonian.
lem-yangian-periodic-monodromy-satisfies:
## Statement

For the chain in [[def-yangian-periodic-fundamental-chain]], let $0,0'$ be two auxiliary copies and define $M_{0'}(v)$ by the same ordered product as $M_0(u)$. For all $u,v\in\mathbb C$,

$$R_{00'}(u-v)M_0(u)M_{0'}(v)=M_{0'}(v)M_0(u)R_{00'}(u-v).$$
thm-yangian-periodic-transfer-matrices-c:
## Statement

For every finite chain in [[def-yangian-periodic-fundamental-chain]], its ordinary un-twisted transfer matrices satisfy $[\tau(u),\tau(v)]=0$ for every $u,v\in\mathbb C$. No genericity condition on the inhomogeneities is needed. The proof uses invertibility only for $u-v\notin\{i,-i\}$ and then extends the resulting polynomial identity to all spectral pairs.
lem-yangian-gl2-one-root-bethe-cancellat:
## Statement

In $Y_i(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ write $A(u)=t_{11}(u)$, $B(u)=t_{12}(u)$, and $D(u)=t_{22}(u)$. Let $\mathcal H$ be a representation with a vector $\Omega$ and scalar-valued functions $a(u),d(u)$, regular at the parameter $v$, such that $A(u)\Omega=a(u)\Omega$, $D(u)\Omega=d(u)\Omega$, and $B(v)\Omega\ne0$. For $u\ne v$, if the one-root Bethe equation $a(v)=d(v)$ holds, then $B(v)\Omega$ is an eigenvector of $A(u)+D(u)$ with eigenvalue

$$\Lambda_v(u)=\frac{u-v-i}{u-v}a(u)+\frac{u-v+i}{u-v}d(u).$$

This one-root cancellation gives no completeness conclusion.
